ideas.reasoning: This directly tests whether structural coverage is more valuable than parameter depth, with the lowest episode budget of the three ideas. Sharing evaluations between arms reduces the cost to at most 270 episodes and four LLM calls, but the result remains conditional on four generated structures rather than establishing generator-wide reliability.
suggested_changes: Preassign generation seed 3500 as the depth control and include it among the four breadth structures, generated with seeds 3500-3503. Share that structure's first six candidate evaluations between arms; depth adds 18 candidates, while breadth evaluates six candidates for each of the other three structures. Each arm still receives 24 candidate evaluations, but execution costs 210 search episodes plus 60 promotion episodes.

Freeze the five-case probe and 30-case promotion manifests under the run out-dir before generation, using seeds 3505-3506 and search root 3507. Keep each placement pool within 50 cases, exclude the final-test split, and select both winners using only the probe.

At up to 605 episodes and four LLM calls, this offers a more direct assembly mechanism test than the task scan, but successful expert-only trajectories may poorly represent the parent's actual handoff states and two edit pairs cannot establish generator-wide reliability.

Include only successful expert continuations in the trace payload; if none succeeds, stop after five episodes with zero generation calls and report inconclusive.

ideas.reasoning: The scan would locate additional failure regimes, but its maximum 1050 episodes and six LLM calls buy a less direct explanation of assembly failure than either intervention above. Its weakest point is confounding contact regime with task identity and one generated structure per task; expert calibration verifies task solvability but does not remove that confounding.
